newsitem.title: CANADA: Nova Scotia may reject Quebec pipeline project.
newsitem.headline: Nova Scotia may reject Quebec pipeline project.

text.p: The province of Nova Scotia may oppose a Quebec-based natural gas pipeline proposal because of political uncertainty in Quebec, Nova Scotia Natural Resources Minister Eleanor Norrie said on Thursday.
Norrie told an oil and gas conference that her government was happy with a rival pipeline group that planned to sell Sable Island gas in the northeastern United States.
The rival consortium, the Maritimes and Northeast Pipeline Group, is headed by Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp 's Panhandle Eastern pipeline unit.
But Norrie said a proposal headed by Montreal-based Gaz Metropolitan and Co and Transcanada Pipelines could be too risky because of the separatist government in Quebec.

"We have concerns about uncertainty in Quebec," Norrie told reporters at the conference. "We have a government in place that has an agenda to separate from the rest of Canada. That uncertainty makes all of Canada uncomfortable, whether it's from the political or business angle. This gives us reason to stop and pause and have concerns about any business that might take place in Quebec."

The Gaz Metropolitan proposal would feed its pipeline system as well as that of TransCanada Pipelines in Quebec." The Maritimes and Northeast route would export gas directly to the United States from New Brunswick.
The Maritimes and Northeast group submitted its formal proposal on Monday. Gaz Metropolitan is expected to follow suit later this month.
